decisions.reason: Confirmed: algebraicity does not imply separability. F_p(u)/F_p(u^p) has minimal polynomial T^p-u^p with zero derivative. Convention 1 now requires algebraic and separable, hence finite under finite generation. Pairwise distinct tuple entries also make the cardinality convention consistent with the set-based definition.

Confirmed erroneous identification: with A=B=Z and C=Z[t], the A-relative functorial map is 0 to C dt, whereas the A'-relative base-change target is zero. Step 2.1 now composes with Omega(C/A) to Omega(C/A'); the localization special case uses V={1}. The tensor inverse calculation and localization fraction formula establish the unchanged three clauses.

The rejection is confirmed: induction and the ideal sequence vary Tor's right-module variable. Replaced F1 with the existing right-variable long exact sequence and supplied a free resolution. Also repaired the independent step 5.1 gap: Artin-Rees on I inside R gives I intersect m^n contained in m^(n-c)I; Krull intersection on the finite S-module I tensor M then kills the kernel. The Koszul consequence uses the already declared AC and regular-sequence supplier.

F2 only defines generators, while regularity of those parameters is the additional theorem already declared as F17. Expanded F17's restatement and cited it before faithfully flat base change in step 2.1. The ascent then lifts regularity successively across nonzerodivisors; descent uses finite syzygies, faithful flat descent of flatness and the residue-field projective-dimension criterion, with dimension zero handled separately.

The maximal ideal of a standard smooth algebra need not contract to the maximal ideal of a local base; R=Z_(p), S=Q demonstrates the gap. Step 1.5 now localizes at the actual contraction before forming the residue fibre. Fibre regular sequences, the graded-piece/Krull argument and the local Tor criterion then prove flatness there; localization transfers it back to the original base. The finite-coefficient descent and unit witness still establish flatness over arbitrary rings.

Confirmed: quotienting the localized fibre gives (K[x]/Q')_g, not K[x]/Q'. The proof now distinguishes the localized minimal prime from its contraction. Its local dimension zero and clause 1 give ht(Q')=c. The quotient domain and its nonzero principal localization have the same fraction field and are finite type, so the published dimension/transcendence-degree theorem gives dimension n-c for the localized component.

Confirmed that the cited binomial theorem is restricted to real numbers. Replaced it with the existing commutative-ring theorem and the prime-divisibility lemma. These imply Frobenius additivity in the characteristic-p field used in step 1.2. The irreducible-factor argument forces degree p when a is not a pth power; the quotient differential presentation gives L dt, while separability makes P'(alpha) invertible and gives zero differentials.

Confirmed that the real binomial theorem does not license Frobenius in L tensor L. The commutative-ring theorem and prime-divisibility lemma now supply it. The functional with lambda(1)=1 and lambda(alpha)=0 proves the tensor difference nonzero; its p-power vanishes. A localization at a maximal ideal containing its annihilator retains this nilpotent, contradicting regular-local domainhood. AC, already required by F4 and Given, is now explicit in the claim.

Confirmed the binomial citation mismatch and replaced it with the ring theorem plus prime-divisibility lemma. Moved the unsupported irreducibility assertion out of F1 into a full factor/derivative argument in step 1.1. Taking the second tensor factor as coefficients makes T-alpha correspond to the stated alpha tensor 1 minus 1 tensor alpha. The basis 1,u,...,u^(p-1) proves nonzero nilpotence, and every prime contains u, proving locality.

The geometric-regularity quantifiers are sound, but the orientation cited a definition as though it proved the equivalence. The later theorem thm-ag-standard-smooth-geometric-regularity clause 3 is the actual finite-type field-case equivalence, under its declared AC premise. The corrected Remarks points there and distinguishes definition terminology from the theorem; no load-bearing circular dependency is added.

F1 incorrectly attributed finite presentation only to the fibre definition; it belongs to both definitions. The theorem already assumes finite presentation, so this error did not enlarge its scope. Corrected F1 and supplied the existing Noetherian finite-type implies finitely-presented theorem for the field case. Chart flatness and geometric fibres prove the forward implication; the local-presentation supplier proves the converse, and localization of ideal kernels proves the global form.

The definition requires finite presentation even when standard smoothness is asserted at one prime. Restored that premise in F1 and explicitly checked finite presentation under base change and composition using finite generators and lifted relations. The block Jacobian determinant h*g^(Nd)*h'' is a unit in the composite chart; the pointwise argument localizes at uv. Thus all original stability and relative-dimension assertions remain intact.

The explanatory sentence contradicted the global finite-type hypothesis and is corrected without weakening that hypothesis. Made explicit that f is a morphism of k-schemes, as required for the stated k-linear cotangent map. The converse now establishes regular local rings before choosing parameters and clears denominators of their images in the localized polynomial chart. Independent parameter classes yield the fibre Jacobian minor; the finite-presentation criterion then gives local standard smoothness.

Irreducibility only makes P a nonzero scalar multiple of the monic minimal polynomial; corrected this, which leaves separability unchanged. The proof now derives algebraicity of x_j from a nonvanishing leading coefficient using minimal total degree, then proves independence by transcendence degree before applying primitive Gauss. Coefficient pth roots rule out F in k[X^p]; inseparable-degree multiplicativity gives the strict decrease. In characteristic zero the perfect field needed is k(T).

Confirmed: Spec Q(sqrt(2)) has two automorphisms over Spec Q, so X-compatibility alone is insufficient. Construction now records the K-structure; comparison is unique over both X and Spec K because on every affine tensor product it fixes both factors. Added the common-principal refinement calculation and corrected affine restrictions to use separate denominators in the two rings. Fibres remain Spec(kappa(x) tensor K), and the associativity comparison is unique with the analogous L-compatibility.

downstream_reviews.affected_use: 1.1 Set $K':=k(T)=k(t_1,\dots,t_r)$ and let $\alpha\in K$ with $K=K'(\alpha)$ be separable over $K'$, as supplied by [F2]. Let $P\in K'[X]$ be the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $K'$; by [F3] it is monic and irreducible, and by [F1] and the definition of a separable element $P$ is separable over $K'$. Hence $\gcd(P,P')=1$ by [F4], $P'\ne0$, and the class of $P'$ is invertible modulo $P$, so $P'(\alpha)\ne0$ in the field $K=K'[X]/(P)$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, given]

downstream_reviews.affected_use: 1.2 Preparation of the section. Write $\kappa=k(T)(\alpha)$ with $T=(t_1,\dots,t_r)$ as in [F2] and [F3], and let $P\in k(T)[X]$ be the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $k(T)$; by [F4] and [F5] the polynomial $P$ is monic, irreducible and separable, so $P'(\alpha)\ne0$ by [F6], since $P'$ is nonzero and $\gcd(P,P')=1$ makes its class a unit of $\kappa=k(T)[X]/(P)$. Put $\overline R:=R/\mathfrak m^{2}$, a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^{2}$ and residue field $\kappa$, and write $\pi\colon\overline R\to\kappa$ for the quotient map. Choose $y_1,\dots,y_r,a\in\overline R$ with $\pi(y_i)=t_i$ and $\pi(a)=\alpha$, and let $\varphi_0\colon k[T]\to\overline R$ be the $k$-algebra map with $T_i\mapsto y_i$. It is injective because the $t_i$ are algebraically independent over $k$, so $k[y_1,\dots,y_r]$ is a polynomial ring and every nonzero element $q(y)$ of it is a unit of the local ring $\overline R$, since $\pi(q(y))=q(t)\ne0$ places it outside the maximal ideal. By the universal property of localisation, $\varphi_0$ extends to a $k$-algebra map $\varphi\colon k(T)\to\overline R$, and $\pi\circ\varphi$ is the inclusion $k(T)\hookrightarrow\kappa$ because they agree on the generators $T_i$. [F2, F3, F4, F5, F6]

downstream_reviews.affected_use: 1.1 Running through the finite list $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$ and adjoining an element exactly when it is transcendental over the field generated by the elements already adjoined produces, after finitely many steps, an algebraically independent $S\subseteq K$ over which every $\alpha_i$ is algebraic; then $K$ is algebraic over $k(S)$ and finitely generated over it, hence finite over $k(S)$ by [F3], so $S$ is a transcendence basis and $[K:k(S)]_i$ is defined by [F7]. The set of values $[K:k(T)]_i$, taken over the finite, algebraically independent $T\subseteq K$ with $K/k(T)$ finite, is a nonempty set of natural numbers and therefore has a least element; fix $T=\{x_1,\dots,x_d\}$ attaining it, and note that each such $T$ is a transcendence basis of $K/k$ by [F2]. If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, then $k(T)$ also has characteristic zero, so is perfect by [F4], and $K/k(T)$ is separable by [F5], so $T$ is already a separating transcendence basis. Henceforth assume $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$.
